Lastly, the demonstration of autonomous liquid hydrogen refueling is still in early phases, however baseline designs and safety requirements have been established. Looking at the conceptual operations for autonomous warehouses, a co-bot, or a semiautonomous arm cooperating with a human, is likely the best path forward for this application. The autonomous warehouses will need human supervision, and autonomous refueling with minimal oversight or assistance is likely a practical solution. The study of autonomous refueling of passenger vehicles in Figure 32 shows a decrease in fueling time from 77 to 9 seconds through use of a robotic arm, showing a path to assisted fueling with partial autonomy for increased time savings. Further, modern robotics is rapidly advancing and future efforts that can leverage advanced robotics will likely play a role in hydrogen refueling. 10. Products: none. 11.
